why_the_dispatcher_filter_is_load_bearin.problem: A `Deferred` row records no terminal, so it is STILL pending when the worker sets `state.pending_scan = true` on completion. why_the_dispatcher_filter_is_load_bearin.why_it_is_safe: `ProjectionRuntimeShared::embedder` is fixed for the session's lifetime, so the condition cannot change under the filter. why_the_dispatcher_filter_is_load_bearin.relationship_to_the_worker_check: The `run_projection_job` check is kept as a LOCAL backstop even though the dispatcher filter makes it unreachable in practice. With `EmbedderChoice::None` there is no dense arm, so enrolling would queue embeds that can only retry to a `'failed'` terminal and pollute `projection_failures`. This was NOT theoretical: the first cut of the fix (enrolment inside `project_canonical_node_row`) turned `slice15d_projection_registry::vector_subobject_is_stored_not_built` RED — it opens with `Engine::open` (no embedder) and documents 'no engine is embedding here … readiness derives to Ready'. The gate needs the live embedder, which a free function holding only a `Connection` cannot see, so enrolment moved up to `Engine`. The declaration still PERSISTS without an embedder and GRAFTS on re-apply in a session that has one — the shipped Q6a contract, pinned by `a_declaration_without_a_live_embedder_defers_then_grafts_on_reapply` (which also asserts zero `projection_failures` rows).

decisions_taken_that_the_reviewer_should.title: Late enrolment must run BEFORE `collect_projection_jobs`
decisions_taken_that_the_reviewer_should.detail: `collect_projection_jobs` runs pre-transaction and decides whether `notify_new_work` fires. Caught by the RED 'write-after-declare' shape, and the reason `collect_projection_jobs` now carries an explicit ordering comment.

found_out_of_scope.title: PRE-EXISTING (landed 20c): a node kind outside `resolve_source_type`'s locked set wedges the projection worker forever
found_out_of_scope.detail: `resolve_source_type` accepts ONLY {email, article, paper, meeting, note, todo, doc, edge_fact} (the '6-value HITL lock' plus the `doc` fixture coercion) and returns `EngineError::Storage` for anything else. BOTH of Slice 20c's enrolment paths enrol on the kind actually present in `canonical_nodes` with no such filter (decision D1 enrols every vector-eligible kind in the corpus; late enrolment enrols any newly-written kind). So a workspace holding a node of, say, kind `memo` that declares `searchable→vector` enqueues a job that can never commit: NO `_fathomdb_projection_terminal` row is ever written, `drain` returns `Err(Scheduler)` forever, and `dense_readiness` stays `embedding` forever.
found_out_of_scope.measured: Two throwaway probes on BOTH enrolment paths (declare-then-write, and write-then-declare) with `PROBE drain(10s) = Err(Scheduler)` / `PROBE2 drain(10s) = Err(Scheduler)`, no terminal recorded. found_out_of_scope.why_it_survived_the_workspace_gate: No existing test declares a `searchable→vector` projection over a kind outside the locked set — every fixture uses `doc`.
found_out_of_scope.impact: The barrier still HOLDS (an Err, never a false Ok), so R-20-DR's correctness invariant is not violated. But it is a permanent liveness wedge for any consumer whose entity kinds are not in the locked list — which is most of them (Memex's kinds, for instance). Likely fixes: filter enrolment on `resolve_source_type(kind).is_ok()`, or make the unmappable kind a recorded `failed` terminal instead of an un-committable job.

found_out_of_scope.title: PRE-EXISTING: missed wakeup in `ProjectionRuntime::wait_for_idle` makes `drain` burn its whole timeout after the work is already done
found_out_of_scope.refs: src/rust/crates/fathomdb-engine/src/lib.rs:1218 (`wait_for_idle`) — the `drop(state)` / `database_has_pending_projection_work` / re-lock window; the worker's `state_cvar.notify_all()` at the end of `projection_worker_loop`
found_out_of_scope.detail: `wait_for_idle` releases the state lock to run `database_has_pending_projection_work`, which opens a FRESH SQLite connection (milliseconds). A worker that finishes the LAST job inside that window does its `notify_all()` before the waiter re-acquires the lock. With no further notification the waiter then sleeps the ENTIRE remaining timeout, re-probes at the loop top, sees idle, and returns `Ok`.

found_out_of_scope.impact: Worse than slow: with a SHORT timeout the same window makes `drain` return a SPURIOUS `EngineError::Scheduler` for work that has already completed. Sibling of OOS-3 (which is about the dispatcher never being woken; this one is about the waiter missing the wake).
